name: Dishoom Shoreditch
description: Bombay-inspired cafe serving outstanding Indian cuisine in a beautifully designed space. Their bacon naan roll at breakfast is legendary.
tips: No reservations for groups under 6 at dinner - arrive before 5:30pm or expect a queue. Worth the wait.

name: Padella
description: Handmade pasta dishes at incredibly reasonable prices. The pappardelle with 8-hour beef shin ragu is extraordinary.
tips: No reservations - queue early. Right next to Borough Market, so combine the two.

name: Sketch - The Gallery
description: An Instagram-famous pink afternoon tea in one of London's most visually stunning restaurants. A truly unique dining experience.
tips: Book well in advance. The egg-shaped toilets are an experience in themselves!

name: Flat Iron
description: Exceptional flat iron steak served with a side salad and unlimited creamy bearnaise sauce. Incredible value.
tips: Just one thing on the menu - steak. And it's brilliant. They give you a mini cleaver as a steak knife.

name: Duck & Waffle
description: London's highest restaurant, open 24/7. Famous for its signature duck and waffle dish and stunning City views.
tips: Book a window table for sunset views. Their 3am brunch is legendary.

name: The Wolseley
description: A grand European-style cafe-restaurant in a stunning Art Deco building on Piccadilly. Perfect for a refined breakfast or afternoon tea.
tips: The breakfast is a London institution. Book ahead or try walking in for counter seats.

name: BAO Soho
description: Tiny Taiwanese bun shop serving pillowy gua bao and small plates. A cult favourite with always a queue.
tips: The classic bao is a must. Try the fried Horlicks ice cream.

name: Rules
description: London's oldest restaurant, established in 1798. Traditional British fare including game, pies, and puddings in opulent Edwardian surroundings.
tips: A quintessentially British experience. The steak and kidney pie is legendary.

name: The Palomar
description: Modern Jerusalem cuisine with influences from Southern Spain, North Africa, and the Levant. Vibrant, energetic atmosphere.
tips: Sit at the counter to watch the chefs at work. The polenta Jerusalem-style is unmissable.

name: Beigel Bake, Brick Lane
description: A legendary 24-hour bagel shop serving London since 1974. The salt beef beigel is a London institution.
tips: Open 24/7. The salt beef beigel with mustard is a rite of passage.

name: Hawksmoor Seven Dials
description: Award-winning steakhouse serving the finest British beef in a beautiful converted brewery. Sunday roast is legendary.
tips: The pre-theatre menu is excellent value. Their Sunday roast is one of the best in London.

name: Ceviche Soho
description: Vibrant Peruvian restaurant known for its fresh ceviches, pisco sours, and lively Soho atmosphere.
tips: Start with a pisco sour and share several small plates.

name: Nando's
description: A British high-street staple serving flame-grilled peri-peri chicken. Reliable, affordable, and loved by Londoners.
tips: A quintessential British experience! Unlimited refills on soft drinks.

name: The Ivy
description: Legendary West End restaurant popular with theatre-goers and celebrities. Classic British and international dishes in Art Deco splendour.
tips: Perfect for pre or post-theatre dining. Book well in advance.

name: Maltby Street Market
description: A foodie's paradise tucked under railway arches. Less touristy than Borough Market with incredible artisanal food stalls.
tips: Open Saturdays 10am-5pm and Sundays 11am-4pm. The grilled cheese from Kappacasein is iconic.

name: Ottolenghi Islington
description: Yotam Ottolenghi's flagship restaurant known for vibrant Mediterranean and Middle Eastern inspired cuisine.
tips: The display counter is a feast for the eyes. Great for vegetarians.

name: Poppies Fish & Chips
description: Award-winning traditional fish and chips in a vintage 1940s-style setting. A proper British chippy experience.
tips: Get the cod or haddock with mushy peas and curry sauce.

name: Chin Chin Labs
description: London's first liquid nitrogen ice cream parlour. Watch your ice cream made with theatrical clouds of nitrogen.
tips: The burnt butter caramel is the signature flavour.

name: Blacklock Sunday Roast
description: The legendary all-in Sunday roast — unlimited meat, potatoes, Yorkshire puddings, and gravy for one set price.
tips: The all-in Sunday roast is exceptional value. Book ahead.

name: Brasserie Zedel
description: A grand Parisian brasserie hidden beneath Piccadilly. Stunning Art Deco interiors and incredibly good-value French cuisine. One of London's best-kept secrets.
tips: The prix fixe menu is absurd value for central London. The room feels like 1930s Paris. There's a live jazz bar downstairs too.

name: Barrafina
description: Michelin-starred Spanish tapas at a counter — watch the chefs prepare your food before your eyes. Some of the best tapas outside Spain.
tips: No reservations — queue before opening for the best chance. The tortilla and croquetas are perfection.

name: St. JOHN Smithfield
description: The birthplace of nose-to-tail eating. Fergus Henderson's pioneering restaurant serves bold British food — bone marrow, devilled kidneys, and the legendary doughnut.
tips: The roasted bone marrow with parsley salad is one of London's most iconic dishes. Don't leave without a Madeira doughnut.

name: Hoppers
description: Sri Lankan and South Indian street food in Soho. Named after the bowl-shaped crepes that are the national dish of Sri Lanka.
tips: Try the egg hopper and the bone marrow varuval. Queue early — no reservations at the Soho branch.

name: Gloria
description: An over-the-top 1970s Italian trattoria from Big Mamma Group. Giant portions, incredible pasta, and a decor so kitsch it's cool. Great for groups and celebrations.
tips: The burrata and truffle pizza are showstoppers. Great for birthdays and group celebrations — they'll make it special.

name: Honest Burgers
description: Proper British burgers made with free-range beef, served with rosemary salted chips. Each branch has a unique local special burger.
tips: Ask for the branch-specific special burger. The rosemary salted chips are legendary.

name: Franco Manca
description: Sourdough pizza at prices that seem too good to be true. Started at Brixton Market and became a London institution. Incredible value.
tips: The No. 6 with nduja is a favourite. Pizzas from £6.95. Hard to beat for value anywhere in London.

name: Bleecker Burger
description: Widely regarded as London's best burger. Dry-aged beef patties, American cheese, and that's about it. Simple perfection.
tips: The Angry burger with jalapenos is the move. Their shakes are outstanding too.

name: E Pellicci
description: A Grade II listed East End greasy spoon that's been run by the same Italian family since 1900. Full English breakfasts, proper builders' tea, and genuine London character.
tips: The Kray twins used to eat here. The Art Deco interior is gorgeous. Cash only. Mama Pellicci might hug you.

name: The Golden Hind
description: Classic fish and chips since 1914 in the heart of Marylebone. No frills, just perfectly battered fish and proper chips.
tips: BYO wine with no corkage fee! Over 100 years of perfect fish and chips.

name: Gymkhana
description: Michelin-starred Indian restaurant inspired by the gymkhana clubs of India. The kid goat keema and wild muntjac biryani are extraordinary.
tips: The tasting menu is the way to go. The cocktails are superb too.

name: Smoking Goat
description: Thai BBQ and drinking food inspired by Bangkok's late-night canteens. Charcoal-grilled meats, fiery salads, and creative cocktails.
tips: The fish sauce chicken wings are addictive. Great for group dining and sharing plates.

name: The Barbary
description: Tiny 24-seat counter restaurant serving bold North African and Middle Eastern food. Every dish is cooked over fire right in front of you.
tips: No reservations — queue early. Only 24 seats so the experience is intimate. The Jerusalem-style kebab is unmissable.

name: Kiln
description: Blazingly good Thai food cooked over charcoal and wood in an open kitchen. Bold, fiery flavours from northern Thailand.
tips: The clay pot baked glass noodles and the aged beef massaman are standouts. Counter seating lets you watch the action.

name: Chiltern Firehouse
description: Celebrity hotspot in a converted Victorian fire station. The food is genuinely excellent — not just a scene. Spectacular courtyard terrace in summer.
tips: Great for special occasions and celebrations. The crab doughnut is legendary. You might spot a celebrity.

name: Dinner by Heston Blumenthal
description: Two Michelin star restaurant reimagining historic British recipes with modern techniques. The Meat Fruit (chicken liver parfait disguised as a mandarin) is iconic.
tips: The Meat Fruit starter is a must. Book well in advance. Beautiful Hyde Park views.

name: BRAT
description: Michelin-starred Basque-inspired grill restaurant. Everything cooked over fire — whole turbot, aged beef, and incredible bread. Raw, elemental cooking.
tips: The whole turbot for two is the signature dish. Sit upstairs at the counter to watch the grill in action.

name: Noble Rot
description: A wine bar and restaurant with an exceptional wine list and seasonal British-European cooking. Cosy, intimate, and romantic.
tips: The wine list is one of London's best. Perfect for a romantic dinner or special celebration.

name: The Breakfast Club
description: All-day brunch institution with queues round the block every weekend. American-style pancakes, eggs every way, and epic milkshakes.
tips: Go before 9am on weekends to avoid the queue. The pancake stacks are epic. There's a hidden speakeasy at the back of the Battersea branch.

name: Granger & Co
description: Aussie brunch legend Bill Granger's London outpost. Famous for the world's best ricotta hotcakes and perfectly scrambled eggs.
tips: The ricotta hotcakes with banana and honeycomb butter are legendary. Beautiful light-filled space.

name: Caravan King's Cross
description: All-day dining in a buzzy converted granary building. World-inspired brunch, excellent specialty coffee, and craft cocktails.
tips: The Granary Square location is beautiful in summer with the fountains. Great coffee and brunch cocktails.

name: BOXPARK Shoreditch
description: The world's first pop-up mall made from shipping containers. Street food from around the globe, craft beers, and a lively rooftop bar.
tips: Great for groups — everyone can get different food. The rooftop hosts DJ sets and live music on weekends.

name: Mercato Metropolitano
description: A massive sustainable community food market in a converted church. Italian-led with food stalls from around the world, a cinema, and live events.
tips: Huge space so you'll always find a seat. Great for groups. The wood-fired pizza is excellent. They host live music events.

name: Brigadiers
description: Indian BBQ and bar inspired by the army mess halls of India. Pool tables, arcade machines, and a whisky bar make this perfect for groups.
tips: Perfect for lads' nights — pool tables, big screens for sport, and incredible food. The lamb chops are outstanding.

name: SUSHISAMBA
description: Japanese, Brazilian, and Peruvian fusion on the 38th floor of Heron Tower. Stunning views and theatrical cocktails. A celebration destination.
tips: The glass elevator ride up is an experience. Request a window table. Perfect for birthdays and special occasions.

name: Sexy Fish
description: An outrageously glamorous Asian seafood restaurant in Mayfair. Over-the-top interiors, incredible cocktails, and a late-night DJ set. See and be seen.
tips: Great for hen parties, birthdays, and special celebrations. The cocktails are art. Smart dress code enforced.

name: Blues Kitchen Bottomless Brunch
description: 2 hours of unlimited prosecco, Bloody Marys, or beer with brunch and live blues music. The ultimate group brunch experience.
tips: Perfect for hen parties, stag dos, and birthday groups. Book ahead — very popular on weekends.

name: Tayyabs
description: A legendary Punjabi restaurant that's been packing them in since 1972. BYO, dirt cheap, and the lamb chops are some of the best in London.
tips: BYO with no corkage. The dry lamb chops are legendary. Expect a queue at peak times but it moves fast.

name: Roti King
description: Tiny basement restaurant serving Malaysian roti canai that draws queues down the street. Flaky, buttery roti with rich curries at rock-bottom prices.
tips: The roti canai with dhal is the star. Cash only. Expect to queue but it's worth every minute.

name: Mangal 1
description: Iconic Dalston ocakbasi grill beloved by locals and artists alike. Charcoal-grilled kebabs, fresh salads, and BYO at its finest.
tips: BYO with no corkage. The adana kebab and lamb chops are excellent. A Dalston institution.

name: Silk Road
description: Authentic Xinjiang Chinese cuisine in an unassuming Camberwell setting. Hand-pulled noodles, cumin lamb, and bold Silk Road spices.
tips: The big plate chicken and hand-pulled noodles are must-orders. BYO with a small corkage fee.

name: Lahore Kebab House
description: A Whitechapel institution serving fiery Pakistani grills and curries since 1972. No-frills setting, maximum flavour, tiny prices.
tips: The seekh kebabs and lamb karahi are legendary. BYO. Don't expect fancy decor — come for the food.

name: Keu
description: Authentic Vietnamese pho and banh mi made with love. The beef pho is rich and fragrant, the banh mi crisp and packed with flavour.
tips: The 24-hour pho is deeply flavoured and comforting. Great quick lunch option in Shoreditch.

name: Kanada-Ya
description: Tonkotsu ramen specialists serving some of London's richest, most authentic ramen. The broth is simmered for 18 hours.
address: 64 St Giles High St, London WC2H 8LE
tips: Get the truffle ramen for a luxurious upgrade. Expect a queue at lunchtime — it moves quickly.

name: Bone Daddies
description: Rock and roll ramen bar with loud music and bold Japanese flavours. The tonkotsu ramen is rich and the buns are addictive.
tips: The pork bone ramen and the chicken wings are must-orders. Fun, loud atmosphere.

name: BAO King's Cross
description: The largest BAO outpost with the full range of Taiwanese dishes. A more relaxed experience than the Soho original with no queue.
address: Coal Drops Yard, Stable St, London N1C 4DQ
tips: Same great food as Soho but you can actually book here. The 40-day aged beef bao is incredible.

name: The Regency Cafe
description: A proper 1940s greasy spoon with Art Deco tiles, Formica tables, and orders bellowed across the room. Full English perfection.
tips: Featured in Layer Cake and Pride. The staff shout your order when it's ready — part of the experience.

name: Monty's Deli
description: Authentic Jewish deli serving proper salt beef bagels, matzo ball soup, and chopped liver. A taste of old East End London.
address: Maltby Street Market, Arch 13, London SE1 3PA
tips: The salt beef reuben is exceptional. Only at Maltby Street Market on weekends.

name: Needoo Grill
description: Whitechapel's answer to Tayyabs, serving fiery Pakistani grills at unbeatable prices. Often less of a queue than its famous neighbour.
tips: Many locals prefer it to Tayyabs. The seekh kebabs and nihari are excellent. BYO.

name: Coal Office
description: Israeli-inspired restaurant from chef Assaf Granit in the Coal Drops Yard development. Bold Middle Eastern flavours in a stunning industrial space.
tips: The soft-serve tahini ice cream is legendary. Beautiful Tom Dixon-designed interiors.

name: Circolo Popolare
description: The sister restaurant to Gloria, with walls covered in thousands of bottles and giant portions of Italian food. A visual and culinary feast.
tips: The lemon meringue pizza is an Instagram sensation. Book well ahead or try walk-in at opening time.

name: Pizarro
description: Jose Pizarro's neighbourhood restaurant serving refined Spanish cooking with seasonal ingredients. Warm, inviting atmosphere.
tips: The Iberico pork dishes are exceptional. Great wine list focused on Spain.

name: Berber & Q
description: Middle Eastern-inspired grill house serving bold charcoal-cooked meats, vibrant salads, and excellent cocktails. A Haggerston favourite.
tips: The cauliflower shawarma is a must even for meat lovers. Great weekend brunch too.

name: Smokestak
description: Serious BBQ and smoking in a stripped-back Shoreditch space. Beef brisket smoked for 16 hours and some of the best ribs in London.
tips: The 35-day-aged brisket is the star. The ox cheek doughnut at brunch is incredible.

name: Jose Tapas Bar
description: A tiny standing-room tapas bar from Jose Pizarro. Authentic Spanish bites, excellent sherry, and a buzzy atmosphere.
tips: Mostly standing room only. The cured meats and croquetas are outstanding. Great sherry selection.

name: Morito
description: The younger sibling of Moro, serving Moorish-inspired tapas in a vibrant, colourful space. Incredible small plates packed with flavour.
tips: Share lots of small plates. The deep-fried borek and patatas bravas are outstanding.

name: 10 Greek Street
description: A Soho neighbourhood restaurant serving excellent seasonal European food with a daily-changing menu. Relaxed, unfussy, and consistently great.
tips: No reservations for dinner — arrive early. The daily menu means there's always something new.

name: Andrew Edmunds
description: A candlelit Soho institution since 1985. Handwritten daily menus, excellent wine, and romantic atmosphere in a Georgian townhouse.
tips: One of the most romantic restaurants in Soho. The wine list offers incredible value. Book ahead for dinner.

name: Brawn
description: A modern European neighbourhood restaurant in Columbia Road with excellent natural wines and a daily-changing menu of bold flavours.
tips: Combine with the Sunday Columbia Road Flower Market for a perfect morning. Excellent natural wine list.

name: Cafe Murano
description: Angela Hartnett's elegant Italian restaurant serving refined Northern Italian cooking. Excellent handmade pasta and impeccable service.
tips: The set lunch menu is excellent value. Refined Italian cooking without the stuffiness.

name: Rochelle Canteen
description: Hidden inside an old school bike shed in Arnold Circus, serving simple, seasonal British food. A treasured secret among East London foodies.
address: Rochelle School, Arnold Circus, London E2 7ES
tips: Ring the buzzer on the old school gate to enter. A true hidden gem. Lunch only.

name: St John Bread and Wine
description: The more casual sibling of St John Smithfield. Nose-to-tail cooking, excellent bread, and the famous Madeira cake doughnuts.
tips: The bacon sandwich at breakfast is legendary. Pick up a doughnut from the bakery counter.

name: Lyle's
description: Michelin-starred restaurant serving a daily-changing set menu of refined, seasonal British cooking in a pared-back Shoreditch setting.
address: Tea Building, 56 Shoreditch High St, London E1 6JJ
tips: The set dinner menu is a surprise each evening. Lunch is more affordable a la carte. Minimalist brilliance.

name: The Clove Club
description: One of London's most celebrated restaurants, serving an innovative tasting menu in the old Shoreditch Town Hall. Creative, precise British cooking.
address: Shoreditch Town Hall, 380 Old St, London EC1V 9LT
tips: Book well in advance. The tasting menu is a journey through modern British cuisine at its finest.

name: Manteca
description: Italian nose-to-tail cooking with in-house charcuterie and handmade pasta. A thrilling Shoreditch restaurant that pushes boundaries.
tips: The in-house salumi and handmade pasta are the highlights. One of the most exciting restaurants in London.

name: The River Cafe
description: Legendary Italian restaurant by the Thames that has trained some of London's greatest chefs. Simple, ingredient-driven cooking at its finest.
address: Thames Wharf, Rainville Rd, London W6 9HA
tips: Worth the journey to Hammersmith. The wood-fired oven dishes are exceptional. Beautiful riverside terrace.

name: Cecconi's
description: Elegant Italian restaurant in Mayfair serving classic Venetian-inspired dishes. A Soho House favourite with impeccable service and beautiful Art Deco interior.
tips: Excellent for a power breakfast or elegant dinner. The cicchetti are perfect for sharing.

name: Ember Yard
description: Spanish and Italian tapas cooked over charcoal and wood. Smoky flavours, creative small plates, and an excellent drinks list.
tips: From the Salt Yard group. The smoked dishes are the highlight. Great for sharing.

name: Bocca di Lupo
description: A Soho gem serving regional Italian dishes from every corner of Italy. Counter seating facing the open kitchen is the best way to dine.
tips: Sit at the counter to watch the chefs. Dishes come in small and large sizes — great for sampling. Gelupo gelato shop is next door.

name: Moro
description: Pioneering North African and Spanish restaurant that has been an Exmouth Market institution since 1997. Bold, sun-drenched flavours.
tips: The wood-roasted dishes are exceptional. One of the most influential restaurants of its generation.

name: Sabor
description: Michelin-starred Spanish restaurant split across three floors, each representing a different region of Spain. The counter at the ground-floor asador is thrilling.
tips: The ground-floor counter is the most fun. The suckling pig is extraordinary. Book well ahead.

name: Yauatcha
description: Michelin-starred dim sum restaurant and tea house in Soho. Exquisite dumplings, modern Chinese dishes, and stunning patisserie in a sleek blue-lit space.
tips: The venison puff and scallop shu mai are outstanding. The patisserie counter is incredible — take macarons home.

name: Great Queen Street
description: A proper British gastropub championing seasonal ingredients. Robust, generous cooking — whole roast shoulders, pies, and proper puddings.
tips: The slow-cooked sharing dishes are the stars. Perfect for groups wanting proper British food.

name: The Eagle
description: London's original gastropub, established in 1991. Mediterranean-inspired daily menu with dishes chalked on the board. A legend of British dining.
tips: The place that started the gastropub revolution. The steak sandwich is legendary. No bookings, arrive early.

name: Anchor & Hope
description: A Waterloo gastropub serving bold, gutsy British cooking. Whole roast animals, offal, and hearty dishes in a no-frills pub setting.
tips: No reservations except for Sunday lunch. Queue early for the best shot at a table. The food is worth the wait.

name: Trullo
description: A neighbourhood Italian restaurant in Highbury with handmade pasta, charcoal-grilled meats, and an excellent Italian wine list. Relaxed and welcoming.
tips: The handmade pappardelle with beef shin ragu is outstanding. Great value set lunch menu.

name: Gunpowder
description: Bold, fiery Indian small plates inspired by family recipes. Tiny but mighty — the flavours are extraordinary and unlike typical curry houses.
tips: The spiced venison and vermicelli doughnut, and the Kashmiri lamb chops are must-orders.

name: Hakkasan
description: Michelin-starred modern Chinese cuisine in a dramatic, moody basement setting. Dim sum, Peking duck, and cocktails in dark, seductive surroundings.
tips: The dim sum lunch is more affordable. The Peking duck is carved tableside. The cocktail bar is excellent.

name: Sketch - Lecture Room & Library
description: Two Michelin-starred fine dining in an opulent, maximalist setting. A multi-course journey through French haute cuisine reimagined by Pierre Gagnaire.
tips: A once-in-a-lifetime dining experience. The tasting menu is an event. Dress smartly.

name: Core by Clare Smyth
description: Three Michelin-starred restaurant from the UK's first female chef to hold three stars. Elegant, refined British fine dining at its absolute peak.
tips: The potato and roe dish is a modern classic. Book months in advance. Worth every penny.

name: The Ledbury
description: Two Michelin-starred restaurant serving inventive modern European cuisine. Brett Graham's cooking is precise, creative, and deeply satisfying.
tips: The flame-grilled deer with smoked bone marrow is extraordinary. Book well in advance.

name: Restaurant Gordon Ramsay
description: London's longest-running three Michelin-starred restaurant. Classic French fine dining with impeccable technique and service in an elegant Chelsea setting.
tips: The three-course lunch menu is the most accessible way in. Impeccable service. Jacket required for gentlemen.

name: Alain Ducasse at The Dorchester
description: Three Michelin-starred French haute cuisine in the glamorous Dorchester hotel. Seasonally driven menus with flawless execution and tableside service.
address: The Dorchester, 53 Park Ln, London W1K 1QA
tips: The lunch set menu offers better value. Exquisite trolley service for cheese and desserts.

name: Kitchen Table
description: A two Michelin-starred 20-seat chef's counter hidden behind the Bubbledogs restaurant. An intimate, immersive multi-course experience.
tips: Only 20 seats at the counter — incredibly intimate. Enter through the hot dog restaurant. Book well ahead.

name: The Araki
description: Ultra-exclusive Japanese omakase with just nine seats at the counter. Formerly three Michelin-starred, offering the finest sushi experience in London.
tips: Only 9 seats. One of the most exclusive dining experiences in London. Reserve far in advance.

name: Hide
description: A stunning restaurant from Ollie Dabbous across three floors connected by a sculptural oak staircase. Refined modern cooking with a world-class wine list.
tips: Hide Above for fine dining, Hide Ground for all-day. The wine list has 6,000 bottles. The staircase is breathtaking.

name: A. Wong
description: Two Michelin-starred Chinese restaurant serving extraordinary dim sum and regional Chinese dishes. Chef Andrew Wong reimagines Chinese cuisine with brilliance.
tips: The dim sum lunch is extraordinary. The tasting menu takes you on a tour of China's regions. Book well ahead.

name: Pied a Terre
description: One of London's longest-running fine dining restaurants. Refined French-European cooking in an intimate Fitzrovia townhouse since 1991.
tips: The set lunch is excellent value for this calibre of cooking. Intimate and personal service.

name: The Square
description: Sophisticated modern French restaurant in Mayfair serving refined tasting menus with impeccable technique and presentation.
tips: The set lunch offers excellent value. A Mayfair classic with consistently high standards.

name: Club Gascon
description: Michelin-starred restaurant celebrating the cuisine of Gascony in southwest France. Foie gras, duck, and Armagnac feature heavily.
tips: The foie gras dishes are a revelation. The marble-clad room is elegant. Good value set lunch.

name: Trinity
description: Michelin-starred neighbourhood restaurant in Clapham serving refined modern European cooking. Adam Byatt's cooking is precise and seasonal.
tips: One of south London's finest restaurants. The set lunch is excellent value for Michelin-starred cooking.

name: Chez Bruce
description: A beloved neighbourhood restaurant on Wandsworth Common serving refined Mediterranean-influenced cooking. Regularly voted London's favourite restaurant.
tips: Consistently one of the best restaurants in London. The cheese trolley is legendary. Book well ahead.

name: The Five Fields
description: Michelin-starred restaurant in Chelsea serving immaculate, seasonal British-French cooking. Ingredients from the restaurant's own farm in East Sussex.
tips: Intimate 40-seat room. The tasting menu changes with the seasons. One of London's hidden fine dining gems.

name: Medlar
description: A refined Chelsea neighbourhood restaurant serving excellent modern European cooking. Warm service and a beautifully balanced menu at fair prices.
tips: The set lunch is outstanding value. Warm, personal service. A Chelsea local favourite.

name: La Dame de Pic
description: Anne-Sophie Pic's London outpost in the Four Seasons. Michelin-starred French fine dining with creative, aromatic, and visually stunning dishes.
address: Four Seasons Hotel, 10 Trinity Square, London EC3N 4AJ
tips: The berlingots (stuffed pasta) are a signature. The set lunch is excellent value for this level of cooking.

name: Campania & Jones
description: A charming Italian deli and restaurant on Columbia Road. Authentic southern Italian cooking with ingredients imported directly from Campania.
tips: Perfect after the Columbia Road Flower Market on Sundays. The aubergine parmigiana is outstanding.

name: On The Bab
description: Authentic Korean street food — fried chicken, bibimbap, and Korean tacos at wallet-friendly prices. Fast, flavourful, and fun.
tips: The Korean fried chicken is addictive. Great quick lunch option.

name: Jinjuu
description: Modern Korean restaurant from celebrity chef Judy Joo. Korean fried chicken, bibimbap, and creative cocktails in a stylish Soho setting.
tips: The Korean fried chicken and the ssam wraps are excellent. Fun cocktail menu.

name: Viet Food
description: Authentic Vietnamese street food in the heart of Soho. Fresh pho, crispy spring rolls, and fragrant curries at great prices.
tips: The pho and the summer rolls are excellent. Great value for central Soho.

name: Wahaca
description: Mexican street food chain founded by MasterChef winner Thomasina Miers. Vibrant tacos, tostadas, and mezcal cocktails.
tips: The pork pibil tacos and the churros are must-orders. Good value for the quality.

name: El Pastor
description: Outstanding Mexican tacos and mezcal in a buzzy Borough Market arch. The al pastor taco cooked on a proper trompo is one of London's best bites.
tips: The al pastor taco is legendary. Great mezcal list. Queue at lunch, or book for dinner upstairs.

name: Le Comptoir Robuchon
description: The more accessible sibling of the late Joel Robuchon's empire. Refined French cooking including the famous pomme puree at Mayfair prices.
tips: The mashed potato (pomme puree) is the most famous in the world. Set lunch is excellent value.

name: Lemonia
description: A beloved Primrose Hill Greek restaurant serving generous portions of classic Greek dishes since 1985. A neighbourhood institution.
tips: The charcoal-grilled lamb chops and moussaka are excellent. A Primrose Hill favourite for decades.

name: The Real Greek
description: Modern Greek meze restaurant with a wide selection of sharing plates. Fresh, vibrant flavours at accessible prices.
address: Riverside Level 1, Royal Festival Hall, London SE1 8XX
tips: Great for a pre-theatre meal at the Southbank Centre. Share the meze platters.

name: Comptoir Libanais
description: Colourful Lebanese restaurant and deli serving fresh, authentic Middle Eastern dishes. Wraps, mezze, and tagines at great prices.
tips: Great for a quick, healthy lunch. The mixed mezze platter is excellent value.

name: Maroush
description: Iconic Lebanese restaurant in Mayfair serving authentic grills, mezze, and pastries since 1981. Open late and beloved by London's Middle Eastern community.
tips: Open until 2am. The mixed grill and the baklava are outstanding. A Mayfair staple.

name: Queen of Sheba
description: Authentic Ethiopian restaurant in Kentish Town serving traditional dishes on injera flatbread. Eat with your hands for the full experience.
tips: Order the mixed platter to try everything. Eat with your hands using the injera bread. Great veggie options.

name: Zeret Kitchen
description: A Camberwell favourite for authentic Ethiopian and Eritrean cuisine. Generous portions of stews and salads served on spongy injera.
tips: The vegetarian platter is outstanding. BYO with a small corkage fee.

name: Roti Joupa
description: A Clapham institution serving authentic Trinidadian roti wraps packed with curry goat, chickpeas, and fiery pepper sauce.
tips: The curry goat roti is legendary. Homemade pepper sauce is seriously hot — use cautiously.

name: Fish, Wings & Tings
description: Vibrant Caribbean restaurant in Brixton Village serving jerk chicken, ackee and saltfish, and fresh tropical juices.
address: Brixton Village Market, Coldharbour Ln, London SW9 8PS
tips: The jerk chicken and ackee and saltfish are excellent. Great vibe in Brixton Village.

name: The Ritz - Afternoon Tea
description: The quintessential London afternoon tea experience in the opulent Palm Court. Finger sandwiches, scones, and pastries served with champagne.
tips: Smart dress code — jacket and tie required for gentlemen. Book well in advance. A bucket-list London experience.

name: Claridge's - Afternoon Tea
description: Art Deco glamour and impeccable service at one of London's most iconic hotels. The afternoon tea features delicate pastries and fine teas.
tips: The Art Deco foyer is stunning. Book weeks ahead. Add champagne for the full experience.

name: Fortnum & Mason - Diamond Jubilee Tea Salon
description: Afternoon tea in the elegant top-floor salon of London's most famous food emporium. Over 300 years of tea expertise.
tips: Browse the food halls before or after tea. Their own-blend teas are exceptional.

name: Mildreds
description: London's most beloved vegetarian restaurant since 1988. Creative plant-based dishes from around the world in a buzzy Soho setting.
tips: No reservations at Soho — queue early. Even committed carnivores love it here.

name: The Gate
description: Sophisticated vegetarian restaurant serving creative, globally-inspired dishes. Beautiful presentations and flavours that make you forget about meat.
tips: The aubergine schnitzel is a signature dish. Great for showing meat-eaters how good veggie food can be.

name: Gauthier Soho
description: An entirely vegan fine dining restaurant in a beautiful Georgian townhouse. Alex Gauthier proves that plant-based cooking can be haute cuisine.
tips: London's finest vegan fine dining. The tasting menu is a revelation. Beautiful townhouse setting.

name: The Ivy Chelsea Garden
description: A glamorous all-day restaurant with a beautiful garden terrace. Classic British dishes, excellent brunch, and a see-and-be-seen crowd.
tips: The garden terrace is stunning in summer. Great for weekend brunch.

name: J Sheekey
description: London's most prestigious seafood restaurant, tucked away in a Theatreland alley. Impeccable fish and shellfish since 1896.
tips: Perfect pre or post-theatre. The fish pie is legendary. The Atlantic Bar next door is more casual.

name: Bentley's Oyster Bar & Grill
description: Richard Corrigan's classic Mayfair seafood restaurant. The downstairs oyster bar is one of London's finest, serving pristine shellfish since 1916.
tips: The oyster bar is more casual and fun. The fish and chips are outstanding.

name: Wright Brothers
description: A Borough Market seafood restaurant sourcing directly from their own oyster farm. Fresh, simply prepared fish and excellent oysters.
tips: The oyster happy hour offers great value. Right in the heart of Borough Market.

name: Tonkotsu
description: Authentic Japanese ramen with rich, creamy tonkotsu broth. Gyoza and Japanese sides complete the menu. Fast, satisfying, and affordable.
tips: The gyoza are handmade and excellent. Great quick lunch in Soho.

name: Dinings SW3
description: Hidden Japanese tapas restaurant serving creative small plates that blend Japanese precision with Western flavours. Exquisite sushi and inventive hot dishes.
address: Walton House, Walton St, London SW3 2JH
tips: The Japanese tapas concept is brilliant. The truffle sushi roll is exceptional.

name: Rosa's Thai Cafe
description: Authentic Thai food at great prices. Fresh, vibrant dishes from pad thai to green curry, with a cosy atmosphere.
tips: The pad thai and the massaman curry are excellent. Great value for the quality.

name: Som Saa
description: Bold, authentic Thai cooking in a huge Whitechapel warehouse space. Dishes you won't find at your average Thai restaurant — rich, funky, and fiery.
tips: The curry and larb dishes are outstanding. Order the whole deep-fried sea bass for the table.

name: XU
description: The upmarket sibling of BAO, serving refined Taiwanese cuisine in a beautiful 1930s-Taipei-inspired dining room. Cocktails are superb.
tips: The shou pa chicken and taro dumplings are outstanding. The cocktails are some of Soho's best.

name: Mei Mei
description: Modern Chinese small plates in a stylish Borough setting. Dumplings, noodles, and sharing plates with creative twists on Chinese classics.
tips: The dumplings and dan dan noodles are excellent. Great for a quick Borough Market area lunch.

name: Barshu
description: Fiery Sichuan cuisine in the heart of Chinatown. Mouth-numbing Sichuan peppercorns, chilli oil, and bold flavours for the adventurous eater.
tips: The mapo tofu and dan dan noodles are fiery perfection. Not for the faint-hearted. Bring water.

name: Four Seasons
description: Famous for what many consider the best roast duck in London. No frills Chinatown restaurant where the crispy duck is the undisputed star.
tips: Order the roast duck — it's what you're here for. Queue at peak times but worth it.

name: dim t
description: Pan-Asian restaurant serving dim sum, noodles, and sushi in a stylish setting. Good variety and reliable quality.
tips: Good for groups wanting a mix of Asian cuisines. The dim sum selection is solid.

name: Tandoor Chop House
description: Indian-British hybrid serving tandoor-grilled meats with British sides. Think lamb chops from the tandoor with mint sauce and dripping chips.
tips: The tandoori lamb chops are outstanding. A clever fusion that actually works.

name: Trishna
description: Michelin-starred Indian seafood restaurant serving coastal Indian cuisine. The brown crab with butter pepper and garlic is one of London's great dishes.
tips: The Dorset brown crab is the signature dish and unmissable. The tasting menu is excellent value.

name: Scott's
description: Mayfair's grandest seafood restaurant, a favourite of the rich and famous since 1851. Oysters, lobster, and fish in a glamorous setting.
tips: The terrace on Mount Street is the place to be seen. The plateau de fruits de mer is spectacular.

name: Hawksmoor Air Street
description: The Piccadilly Circus branch of London's finest steakhouse. Art Deco interiors, perfectly aged beef, and outstanding cocktails.
tips: The express lunch menu is excellent value. The bar serves some of London's best cocktails.

name: Goodman
description: A Mayfair steakhouse specialising in USDA and British beef aged on-site. Serious steak for serious steak lovers.
tips: Choose your cut at the meat trolley. Both USDA and British options available. Excellent mac and cheese side.

name: Blacklock
description: Skinny chops, big chops, and pre-theatre deals in a former underground strip club. Simple concept, brilliantly executed, at great prices.
tips: The all-in chop deal is incredible value. Great pre-theatre option at just a few pounds.

name: Where The Pancakes Are
description: A dedicated pancake restaurant serving Dutch-style pancakes all day. Sweet, savoury, and everything in between.
tips: The Dutch baby pancake is a showstopper. Great for brunch near Borough Market.

name: Sunday
description: A bright and airy brunch spot on Barnsbury Street. Eggs, pancakes, and shakshuka served in a relaxed neighbourhood setting.
tips: Perfect lazy weekend brunch spot. The shakshuka is outstanding.

name: Dishoom King's Cross
description: The grandest Dishoom, set in a spectacular converted transit shed. The breakfast naan roll and black daal are essential London experiences.
tips: The only Dishoom that takes breakfast reservations. The bacon naan roll is legendary. The space is stunning.

name: Pizza Pilgrims
description: Neapolitan pizza made in Fior di Latte ovens shipped from Naples. Puffy, charred crusts and quality toppings at fair prices.
tips: The nduja honey pizza is a cult favourite. Great for a quick, delicious Soho lunch.

name: Cay Tre
description: Authentic Vietnamese cuisine in Shoreditch. Fragrant pho, crispy banh xeo pancakes, and vibrant salads in a stylish setting.
tips: The pho and the banh xeo are standouts. Great value for the quality.

name: Persepolis
description: A Persian grocery and cafe in Peckham serving authentic Iranian dishes. Homely, welcoming, and packed with flavour.
tips: Browse the Persian grocery while you wait. The lamb stews and rice dishes are authentic and delicious.

name: Burger & Lobster
description: Simple concept done well — choose from a burger, a lobster, or a lobster roll. All served with fries and salad at a set price.
tips: The original lobster roll is hard to beat. Great value for Mayfair.

name: Five Guys
description: American burger chain with a cult following. Customisable burgers, hand-cut fries, and free peanuts while you wait.
tips: The regular fries are huge — a small is more than enough. Free toppings on all burgers.

name: Patty & Bun
description: Some of London's most flavour-packed burgers. The Ari Gold burger with smoky bacon, pickled onions, and special sauce is legendary.
tips: The Ari Gold is the signature — smoky, messy, and brilliant. Great shakes too.

name: NOPI
description: Ottolenghi's upmarket Soho restaurant. Refined Middle Eastern and Asian-inspired sharing plates in a bright, marble-clad space.
tips: More refined than the delis but equally vibrant. The burrata with burnt aubergine is outstanding.

name: Darjeeling Express
description: Chef Asma Khan's celebrated Indian restaurant serving Mughlai royal family recipes. As seen on Netflix's Chef's Table. An all-female kitchen.
tips: The goat biryani is legendary. Order the thali for a taste of everything. All-female kitchen team.

name: Sketch - The Parlour
description: A whimsical patisserie and tearoom at ground level in Sketch. Exquisite pastries, afternoon tea, and cocktails in a fantastical pink setting.
tips: More accessible and affordable than the Gallery upstairs. The pastries are works of art.

name: BAO Noodle Shop
description: The noodle-focused sibling of BAO, serving hand-pulled noodles, dumplings, and Taiwanese beef noodle soup. Quick and satisfying.
tips: The beef noodle soup is rich and deeply flavoured. Quick service — great for a fast Shoreditch lunch.

name: The Foley
description: A stylish Fitzrovia pub serving elevated gastropub food. Seasonal British dishes, craft beers, and a great wine list in a relaxed setting.
tips: Great neighbourhood gastropub. The Sunday roast is excellent.

name: Townsend
description: A bright, all-day restaurant in the Whitechapel Gallery serving seasonal British food. Beautiful space with a focus on simplicity and quality ingredients.
address: Whitechapel Gallery, 77-82 Whitechapel High St, London E1 7QX
tips: Combine with a visit to the Whitechapel Gallery. The daily-changing menu focuses on seasonal ingredients.

name: The Shed
description: A Notting Hill restaurant run by three farming brothers, serving produce from their family farm in West Sussex. Rustic, seasonal, and genuine.
tips: Farm-to-table genuinely. The slow-cooked dishes are highlights. A Notting Hill local favourite.

name: Chick 'n' Sours
description: Fried chicken and sour cocktails in a fun, no-frills setting. Seriously good Korean-inspired fried chicken with creative sides.
tips: The fried chicken is crispy perfection. The sour cocktails are addictive. Great fun atmosphere.

name: Salvation in Noodles
description: A tiny Dalston Vietnamese cafe serving enormous bowls of pho at tiny prices. Authentic and beloved by the Vietnamese community.
tips: The pho is outstanding and enormous. Cash only. One of the best value meals in London.

name: Bibimbap
description: Quick-service Korean restaurant specialising in the namesake rice bowl dish. Customise your toppings and enjoy authentic Korean flavours.
tips: Get the hot stone bibimbap for the crispy rice at the bottom. Quick, cheap, and satisfying.

name: Lupita
description: Authentic Mexican restaurant near Charing Cross serving tacos, enchiladas, and mezcal cocktails. More refined than your average taqueria.
tips: The mole dishes are excellent. Great mezcal selection.

name: Le Bab
description: Gourmet kebabs from a Michelin-trained team. Shawarma, doner, and shish reimagined with premium ingredients and creative toppings.
address: Kingly Court, 4 Kingly Ct, London W1B 5PW
tips: Kebabs reimagined — the lamb shawarma is outstanding. Proof that kebabs can be gourmet.

name: The Haberdashery
description: A quirky, vintage-styled cafe in Stoke Newington serving excellent brunch and cake. Mismatched furniture, board games, and all-day vibes.
tips: The cakes are homemade and excellent. Lovely relaxed vibe with board games and vintage decor.

name: Petersham Nurseries Cafe
description: A magical greenhouse restaurant in Richmond serving seasonal Italian-influenced food among the plants. One of London's most romantic settings.
address: Church Ln, Off Petersham Rd, Richmond TW10 7AB
tips: One of the most beautiful dining settings in London. Lunch only. Book well in advance.

name: Spring
description: Skye Gyngell's light-filled restaurant in Somerset House. Ingredient-driven Italian-influenced cooking in one of London's most beautiful dining rooms.
address: Lancaster Place, New Wing, Somerset House, London WC2R 1LA
tips: The dining room is stunning with natural light. The set lunch is excellent value. Beautiful courtyard in summer.

name: Sardine
description: A southern French and Italian neighbourhood restaurant in a former warehouse. Simple, seasonal cooking focused on vegetables, fish, and fire.
tips: The wood-roasted dishes are the stars. Relaxed and unpretentious. A Hoxton gem.

name: Sessions Arts Club
description: A stunning restaurant in a former courtroom on Clerkenwell Green. Seasonal European cooking in one of London's most dramatic dining rooms.
tips: The crumbling, beautiful room is unforgettable. Book well ahead. One of London's most talked-about restaurants.

name: Flor
description: A restaurant from the team behind Lyle's, serving wood-fired dishes and exceptional natural wines above Borough Market. Mediterranean-inspired menu.
tips: The bakery downstairs sells incredible sourdough. The wine list is outstanding.

name: Jolene
description: A bakery-restaurant in Newington Green serving incredible sourdough, seasonal British food, and natural wines. All-day dining with a neighbourhood feel.
tips: The sourdough bread is some of the best in London. Great for breakfast or a relaxed lunch.

name: Cafe Cecilia
description: Max Rocha's beautiful Hackney canal-side restaurant serving hearty, seasonal dishes with an Irish and European influence. Warm and nurturing cooking.
tips: The soda bread and the daily-changing menu are highlights. A restaurant with real soul.

name: Mangal 2
description: A Dalston ocakbasi grill that was a favourite of the late Anthony Bourdain. Charcoal-grilled Turkish meats at excellent prices.
tips: Anthony Bourdain was a regular. BYO wine. The mixed grill is outstanding value.

name: Orasay
description: A refined seafood restaurant in Notting Hill inspired by the Scottish Hebrides. Elegant, coastal-inspired dishes with impeccable sourcing.
tips: The whole roasted fish is the star. From the Brat team. Beautiful Notting Hill setting.

name: Pavyllon London
description: Yannick Alleno's London restaurant at the Four Seasons, serving modern French cuisine with theatrical counter seating and an open kitchen.
address: Four Seasons Hotel, Hamilton Pl, London W1J 7DR
tips: Sit at the counter to watch the chefs. The sauce work is extraordinary. Set lunch offers good value.

name: Masala Zone
description: Vibrant Indian street food and thalis at wallet-friendly prices. A reliable chain for satisfying, flavourful Indian food across London.
tips: The thalis are excellent value and give you a taste of everything. Good for groups.

name: Oka
description: Refined Japanese restaurant on Kingsland Road serving excellent sushi, robata grill items, and creative cocktails. Sleek and stylish.
tips: The sushi and the robata-grilled dishes are highlights. A more refined alternative on Kingsland Road.

name: Perilla
description: A modern European neighbourhood restaurant in Newington Green. Creative tasting menus and a la carte with brilliant natural wines.
tips: The tasting menu is a steal for this quality. A gem of the north London dining scene.

name: The Marksman
description: A Michelin-starred pub in Hackney Road. The beef and barley bun is legendary, and the cooking elevates pub food to an art form.
tips: The beef and barley bun is a must. A Michelin-starred pub — drink a pint downstairs and dine upstairs.

name: The Duck & Rice
description: A Chinese gastropub in Soho, combining craft beer and cocktails with Cantonese-inspired dishes. Alan Yau's casual dining concept.
tips: The crispy duck salad and dim sum are excellent. Great pub atmosphere with a Chinese twist.

name: Taberna do Mercado
description: Nuno Mendes' Portuguese tapas bar in Spitalfields Market. Petiscos, Portuguese wines, and pasteis de nata in a charming market setting.
tips: The croquettes and the custard tarts are outstanding. A lovely spot inside Spitalfields Market.

name: Kudu
description: A South African-inspired restaurant in Peckham. Creative dishes blending South African and European influences with locally sourced ingredients.
tips: The braai-grilled dishes are superb. A rising star of the south London dining scene.

name: Norman's
description: A cosy, no-booking Tufnell Park restaurant that feels like eating in someone's home. Seasonal Mediterranean cooking and natural wines.
tips: No bookings — arrive early. Feels like eating in a friend's kitchen. Natural wines are excellent.

name: Santa Maria Pizzeria
description: Award-winning Neapolitan pizza in Ealing — worth the journey from central London. The dough is fermented for 48 hours for maximum flavour.
tips: Many say it's the best pizza in London. The pilgrimage to Ealing is worth it. BYO.

name: My Neighbours The Dumplings
description: Handmade Chinese dumplings in a fun, communal Hackney setting. Pork and chive, prawn, and creative seasonal fillings at great prices.
tips: The dumplings are handmade fresh. BYO wine. A Clapton favourite.

name: Peckham Bazaar
description: A colourful Peckham restaurant celebrating the food of the Balkans, Middle East, and Eastern Mediterranean. Open fire cooking and vibrant flavours.
tips: Everything cooked over fire. The lamb dishes are exceptional. Great natural wine list.

name: Planque
description: A wine-focused restaurant in Hackney serving modern European dishes with an emphasis on natural wines. Beautiful arch setting.
tips: The wine list is exceptional. The sharing plates are designed for groups. Under a railway arch.

name: Gokyuzu
description: A massive Turkish ocakbasi grill on Green Lanes. Enormous portions of perfectly charcoal-grilled meats at absurdly low prices.
tips: Huge portions and tiny prices. The mixed grill platter is enormous. BYO. Always busy — expect a short wait.

name: Kricket
description: Modern Indian small plates that push boundaries. Inventive, spice-led cooking that reimagines Indian food for London. Counter dining in Soho.
tips: The samphire pakoras and the Keralan fried chicken are outstanding. Modern Indian at its best.

name: Isabel
description: A glamorous Mayfair restaurant and bar serving Mediterranean and Latin American-inspired dishes. Beautiful interiors and a buzzy late-night scene.
tips: Great for a glamorous night out. The cocktails are excellent. Smart dress code.

name: Sagar
description: South Indian vegetarian restaurant serving outstanding dosas, idli, and thalis. Authentic, affordable, and beloved by London's vegetarian community.
tips: The masala dosa is enormous and delicious. Some of the best value vegetarian food in central London.

name: Jin Kichi
description: An authentic Japanese izakaya in Hampstead. Yakitori grilled over charcoal, sashimi, and Japanese small plates in a cosy, neighbourhood setting.
tips: The yakitori is outstanding — grilled to perfection. A Hampstead favourite for decades.

name: Kanada-Ya Piccadilly
description: The Piccadilly branch of the celebrated ramen chain. Rich 18-hour tonkotsu broth, springy noodles, and flavour-packed toppings.
tips: Central location for a quick ramen fix. The truffle ramen is worth the upgrade.

name: Som Saa Thai Noodles
description: Quick Thai noodle dishes from the Som Saa team. Bold, authentic flavours in a casual setting. Fast, fiery, and affordable.
tips: From the team behind Som Saa. Quick, authentic Thai noodles at market prices.

name: Baozi Inn
description: Authentic Sichuan street food in Chinatown. Fiery dan dan noodles, steamed bao, and cold Sichuan dishes in a no-frills setting.
tips: The dan dan noodles and the cold spicy pork are must-orders. Tiny and always busy.

name: The Manor
description: A refined neighbourhood restaurant in Clapham Common. Creative modern European dishes with seasonal British ingredients.
tips: The tasting menu is excellent value. A south London hidden gem.

name: Hunan
description: A unique leave-it-to-the-chef Chinese restaurant in Pimlico. No menu — Mr Peng sends out dish after dish of Hunanese and Sichuanese cooking.
tips: No menu — just tell them what you don't eat and the kitchen decides. A totally unique dining experience.

name: Koya
description: Exceptional handmade udon noodles in a simple, no-frills Soho setting. Hot or cold broth, perfectly chewy noodles, and clean Japanese flavours.
tips: The hot udon in dashi broth is soul food. Simple, perfect, and affordable.

name: Fatt Pundit
description: Indo-Chinese street food from Kolkata's Chinatown. A unique cuisine you won't find anywhere else in London — chilli paneer, Hakka noodles, and momos.
tips: A cuisine you won't find elsewhere. The chilli chicken and momos are excellent.
